A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Shop-R1 and contain readable text, equations, figures, tables and complete appendices. The retained experiments and prompts can be matched reliably across versions.

before.justification: V1 reports original shopping-action prediction experiments, baseline comparisons and ablations in Section 4, Tables 2–5 and Figure 2.

after.justification: V2 retains those original experiments and adds an OPeRA evaluation in Appendix E, Table A3.

M1.justification: The SFT-to-GRPO pipeline, hierarchical rewards, self-certainty reward and difficulty-aware scaling are retained. Equation (1) drops historical rationales, aligning the formulation with the context/action inputs already described for RL in v1; no changed operational procedure is established.

E1.justification: V2 adds evaluation on the public OPeRA dataset, covering 692 human shopping sessions and input, click and scroll actions. This substantially extends evidence beyond the original corpus. Naming that retained 52,137-session corpus SHOP-CART does not itself add coverage.

E2.justification: Appendix E newly evaluates Claude-3.5-Sonnet as a zero-shot comparator; v1 used it for rationale generation without reporting this baseline evaluation. The comparator set in the original main experiments is unchanged.

E3.justification: The added OPeRA experiment uses Qwen2.5-VL-3B-Instruct with 8,212 training and 1,508 testing examples. Existing training budgets, model configurations and metrics remain unchanged. Newly disclosed original-corpus split counts do not establish a changed split.

E4.justification: The model-size, temperature, training-component and context ablations are retained without new analysis designs. OPeRA adds benchmark evaluation rather than a controlled robustness or transfer test. The isolated Table 4 numerical update is assessed under E6.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental seed counts, repeated-run variability, confidence intervals or significance tests. The variances introduced in Appendix A concern mathematical reward normalization, not uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: Table A3 adds OPeRA results: Shop-R1 achieves 38.44% exact-action accuracy versus SFT's 20.23%, while action-type accuracy falls from 60.86% to 57.27% and F1 rises from 53.95% to 57.69%. These are new benchmark results, not improvements over v1 under identical conditions. Table 4 also changes the binary-action-reward ablation from 27.41% to 27.04%; Tables 2, 3 and 5 retain their percentages.

T1.justification: New Appendix A derives invariance of GRPO standardized advantages under positive affine reward transformations and supplies a four-sample numerical example. V1 has no corresponding proof. Equation (1) also revises the formal task inputs by removing historical rationales.

C1.justification: The first contribution narrows the claimed novelty from introducing RL into simulation-oriented human behavior modeling generally to doing so in web-shopping environments. The framework contribution and headline 27.72% versus 16.76% accuracy claim remain unchanged.

C2.justification: V2 newly explains that persona and intent are unobserved and frames the task as modeling behavioral tendencies rather than recovering latent psychological states. It also characterizes reward weights as page-independent normalization constants and interprets OPeRA results as evidence of generality.

D1.justification: Appendix C newly discloses 176,949 training and 1,879 testing examples and per-action counts for the original corpus; Appendix E supplies OPeRA counts. A project-page link replaces v1's promise to release code and checkpoints upon acceptance. Existing hardware, hyperparameters and substantive prompt content are retained.

R1.justification: V2 adds citations including GenTUS, USimAgent, WebServ and Customer-R1, and sharpens its distinction from goal-specified task-completion agents. The main related-work organization and positioning remain intact; citation-style changes are not substantive additions.

P1.justification: Most main-text prose and the section sequence are retained. V2 adds focused explanations and an LLM writing-assistance statement, updates affiliations and citation style, and relabels the existing prompt appendices within an expanded appendix structure.

P2.justification: V2 adopts ICLR formatting, reflows and resizes existing displays, expands Figure 1's caption and corrects Table 3's model labels. It adds Tables A1–A3 for dataset statistics and OPeRA results, while retaining the existing figures and main-table structures.

improvement.justification: The public OPeRA evaluation broadens v1's private-corpus-only evidence, and the added split and action counts improve transparency. These provide a limited net gain: the new evaluation setup remains briefly documented, and Appendix A overstates its positive-affine invariance proof by concluding that preserving reward rankings alone suffices.
